phrase.text: Every run ends in one of six states: it finished well, it failed, it is waiting for input, it is waiting for the outside world, it was cancelled or it ran out of a limit.

runs.text: Every run ends in one of six states: it finished well, it failed, it is waiting for input, it is waiting for the outside world, it was cancelled or it ran out of a limit.
When a program stops moving forward, the engine says exactly why. That reason is called the
and it is always one of these six:

rows.text: needs a value that has not arrived yet
It is waiting for an answer from a file, clock or network
Whoever was running it stopped it
It ran out of a statement, memory or depth budget

blocks.description: At the top, the running state. An arrow goes down to a box with the four final terminations: completed, failed, cancelled and limit_reached. Two side arrows lead to the pauses awaiting_input and awaiting_effect, which resume.

caption.text: From "running" one of six states is reached. Two of them are pauses you can come back from.

runs.text: A runtime failure stops the program at the exact statement. What was already written is kept:

blocks.title: Ends with a failure

runs.text: receives no value, the program pauses. The editor asks you for the data and the run continues where it stopped:

blocks.title: Waits for input

runs.text: are final: no more effects happen after them. The pauses
resume at exactly the statement where they stopped.

points.text: A failure stops the program at the exact statement and keeps what was already written.
